summary.one_liner: yagmail is a Python client that makes sending emails over Gmail/SMTP simple, with automatic handling of text, HTML, images and attachments, plus a built-in asyncio client.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a yagmail.Client class that connects to a Gmail or SMTP server and sends emails with a single send() call. The "magical contents" feature guesses whether each item is a local file to attach or inline, an HTML string, or plain text. Recipients can be a single address, a list, or a dict mapping addresses to aliases, and omitting "to" sends to yourself. Attachments can be given as file paths or as io.IOBase objects, and images can be placed inline in the body. It also supports OAuth2 authentication, DKIM signing via a DKIM helper class, and an AsyncClient built on standard library asyncio streams. A command-line interface is mentioned as also available.
use_cases: send email from a Python script
email files attached to a message
send emails to a list of recipients with aliases
send automated reports or notifications via Gmail
notable: Magical contents: automatically decides whether each item is a file to attach, inline HTML, or text
OAuth2 authentication option with revocable tokens
Supports DKIM signing with a private key
Recipients can be given aliases via a dict
caveats: For Gmail, regular account passwords no longer work; an Application-Specific Password or OAuth2 is needed
OAuth2 tokens expire after 7 days unless the Google Cloud project's consent screen is In production
Connections may not close automatically on PyPy, so the with statement is recommended there
